f.title: Investigate any communicable-disease adverse reaction related to a distributed HCT/P
f.statement: The establishment must investigate any adverse reaction involving a communicable disease related to an HCT/P that it made available for distribution.
f.applicability: Nonreproductive HCT/Ps described in 1271.10 and regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act (Subpart E applicability, 1271.330)
f.processes: Safety intake & collection; Medical review; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Report to FDA communicable-disease adverse reactions that are fatal, life-threatening, permanently impairing or need intervention
f.statement: The establishment must report to FDA an adverse reaction involving a communicable disease if it is fatal; is life-threatening; results in permanent impairment of a body function or permanent damage to body structure; or necessitates medical or surgical intervention, including hospitalization.
f.applicability: Nonreproductive HCT/Ps described in 1271.10 and regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act (Subpart E applicability, 1271.330)

to FDA an adverse reaction involving a
communicable disease if it:
(i) Is fatal;
(ii) Is life-threatening;
(iii) Results in permanent impairment of a body function or permanent
damage to body structure; or
(iv) Necessitates medical or surgical
intervention, including hospitalization.

f.title: Submit each adverse reaction report on Form FDA 3500A within 15 calendar days of initial receipt
f.statement: The establishment must submit each adverse reaction report on Form FDA 3500A to the address in 1271.350(a)(5) within 15 calendar days of initial receipt of the information.
f.applicability: Nonreproductive HCT/Ps described in 1271.10 and regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act (Subpart E applicability, 1271.330)

f.statement: The establishment must, as soon as practical, investigate all adverse reactions that are the subject of these 15-day reports.

f.title: Submit follow-up reports within 15 calendar days of new information or as FDA requests
f.statement: The establishment must submit followup reports within 15 calendar days of the receipt of new information or as requested by FDA.

f.title: Describe the steps taken when additional follow-up information cannot be obtained
f.statement: If additional information is not obtainable, a followup report may be required that briefly describes the steps taken to seek additional information and the reasons why it could not be obtained.

f.title: Submit two copies of each adverse reaction report to CBER
f.statement: The establishment must submit two copies of each adverse reaction report to FDA CBER Document Control Center at the address given; FDA may waive the requirement for the second copy in appropriate circumstances.

f.title: Investigate HCT/P deviations for distributed HCT/Ps where you performed a manufacturing step
f.statement: The establishment must investigate all HCT/P deviations related to a distributed HCT/P for which it performed a manufacturing step.
f.applicability: Nonreproductive HCT/Ps described in 1271.10 and regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act (Subpart E applicability, 1271.330)

rows.quote:
(b) Reports of HCT/P deviations. (1)
You must investigate all HCT/P deviations related to a distributed HCT/P
for which you performed a manufacturing step.

f.title: Report core-CGTP HCT/P deviations in your own or contract facilities, with description and follow-up actions
f.statement: The establishment must report any such HCT/P deviation relating to the core CGTP requirements if it occurred in its facility or in a facility that performed a manufacturing step for it under contract, agreement or other arrangement; each report must describe the deviation, information relevant to the event and the manufacture of the HCT/P, and all follow-up actions taken or to be taken (e.g. recalls).
f.applicability: Nonreproductive HCT/Ps described in 1271.10 and regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act (Subpart E applicability, 1271.330)

f.title: Report each core-CGTP HCT/P deviation on Form FDA 3486 within 45 days of discovery
f.statement: The establishment must report each HCT/P deviation relating to a core CGTP requirement on Form FDA 3486 within 45 days of the discovery of the event, either electronically through the CBER web-based application or by mail to the CBER Document Control Center.
